import pytest from playwright.sync_api import Page import re
def test_sort_by_name_a_to_z_alternative_approach(page: Page): """ Alternative test approach using more flexible selectors and error handling. """
try: # Navigate directly to cameras with potential Apple filter page.goto("https://ecommerce-playground.lambdatest.io/index.php?route=product/category&path=33") page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")
# Try to apply Apple filter if available try: apple_checkbox = page.locator("input[type='checkbox'][value*='Apple'], input[name*='Apple']").first if apple_checkbox.count() > 0 and apple_checkbox.is_visible(): apple_checkbox.check() page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle") except Exception as e: print(f"Error applying Apple filter: {e}")
# DEBUG: Print all select elements' outer HTML to diagnose dropdown selectors all_selects = page.locator('select') print(f"Found {all_selects.count()} select elements on the page:") for i in range(all_selects.count()): print(all_selects.nth(i).evaluate('el => el.outerHTML'))
# Use a robust selector for the sort dropdown (id starts with input-sort) sort_element = page.locator("select[id^='input-sort']") assert sort_element.count() > 0 and sort_element.is_visible(), "Sort dropdown not found" sort_element = sort_element.first
# Select sort by name A-Z by value for reliability # Find the value for Name (A - Z) options = sort_element.locator('option') value = None for i in range(options.count()): opt = options.nth(i) if 'Name (A - Z)' in opt.text_content(): value = opt.get_attribute('value') break assert value, 'Could not find value for Name (A - Z) option' sort_element.select_option(value=value) page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")
# Get product names using the most flexible approach product_elements = page.locator(".product-thumb h4, .product-item h4, h4").filter(has_text=re.compile(r".+"))
names = [] for i in range(product_elements.count()): element = product_elements.nth(i) link = element.locator("a").first if link.count() > 0 and link.is_visible(): name = link.text_content().strip() if name and len(name) > 1: names.append(name)
# Verify sorting assert len(names) >= 2, f"Need at least 2 products to test sorting, found {len(names)}"
sorted_names = sorted(names, key=lambda x: x.lower()) assert names == sorted_names, f"Products not sorted: {names} vs {sorted_names}"
print(f"✓ Successfully verified {len(names)} products are sorted A-Z")
except Exception as e: page.screenshot(path="sort_test_failure.png") raise e
def test_sort_by_name_a_to_z_sorting(page: Page): """ Test that products are sorted by Name A-Z in the cameras category. """ # Go directly to the cameras category page.goto("https://ecommerce-playground.lambdatest.io/index.php?route=product/category&path=33") page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")
# Use a robust selector for the sort dropdown (id starts with input-sort) sort_element = page.locator("select[id^='input-sort']") assert sort_element.count() > 0 and sort_element.is_visible(), "Sort dropdown not found" sort_element = sort_element.first
# Select sort by name A-Z by value for reliability options = sort_element.locator('option') value = None for i in range(options.count()): opt = options.nth(i) if 'Name (A - Z)' in opt.text_content(): value = opt.get_attribute('value') break assert value, 'Could not find value for Name (A - Z) option' sort_element.select_option(value=value) page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")
# Extract product names from the page product_names = page.locator(".product-thumb h4 a, .product-item h4 a").all_text_contents() product_names = [name.strip() for name in product_names if name.strip()]
assert len(product_names) > 1, "Not enough products found to test sorting."
# Check if the list is sorted alphabetically (case-insensitive) sorted_names = sorted(product_names, key=lambda x: x.lower()) assert product_names == sorted_names, f"Products are not sorted A-Z. Actual: {product_names}"
if __name__ == "__main__": pytest.main([__file__, "-v"])
